title: Remainder Tower Cards
question: Order the four violet cards by their one to four amber dots. On each card, replace each tower by a dark square when its height in boxes is a multiple of three, otherwise by a pale square. Use the four results as rows of a 4 by 4 tile. Which symbol appears: hourglass, diamond, falling blocks, or rising blocks?

task_signature.mechanism: Decode tower-height divisibility on four visibly ranked detached cards, then stack the decoded rows and classify the raster symbol.

latent_z.description: Four shuffled, widely separated cards whose unit-box tower heights encode balanced rows through divisibility by three.

latent_alias.justification: The sampled fields all change visible pixels when changed, and no nontrivial pixel-identical latent alias is asserted for this discrete card renderer.

boundary.observable: The runner-up boundary is the pixel-recovered Hamming-distance gap between the decoded 4 by 4 tile and the four declared templates.
boundary.quarantine: A scene is quarantined if a tower is not an integral three- or four-box stack, a card rank is missing or repeated, or the template margin is below eight cells.

semantic_contrast.contrast: Unlike cyclic-row rectification, no row is already present as a shifted binary raster and no cell marker declares a cyclic phase; the card dots bind whole cards only after each unary tower has been arithmetically reduced. Unlike height-tab sorting, tower heights are not rank keys and no source strip is moved. Unlike tooth-route rasterization, evidence is four disconnected ranked cards rather than signs along one path. Unlike punch-card parity or the modular loom, no aligned masks are combined and no outer arithmetic field is synthesized.
semantic_contrast.expected_information_gain: Isolates whether a model can bind distant card ranks, count discrete tower units, apply a declared arithmetic predicate repeatedly, and reassemble the resulting rows without relying on aggregate ink.
